pain.title: The costliest mistakes when buying at auction cost more than the training
pain.subtitle: This isn't theory. These are real losses we see in beginners every week.
items: Bought a car cheaper but ignored shipping, fees, port, repair and paperwork
Trusted the photos but didn't check VIN, history, seller and prior bids
Didn't understand the title and bought a car that's hard or impossible to register cleanly
Set the wrong max bid and burned the margin
Didn't grasp which states and auctions are friendlier for logistics
Bought a car with damage that looks light but is expensive to repair
Had no checklist and decided emotionally
Paid a broker without understanding exactly what they're paying for

titleGuide.title: The title decides whether the car is a good buy or a problem
titleGuide.subtitle: The course has a dedicated module on titles, states and documents. It's one of the most critical economic factors.

items.name: Clean Title
items.desc: Doesn't automatically mean an ideal car, but it's usually the simpler document for downstream registration.

items.name: Salvage Title
items.desc: Can be repairable, but requires understanding the damage, state rules and future registration.

items.name: Rebuilt / Former Salvage
items.desc: The car has already gone through restoration. You need the full history and quality of prior repair.

items.name: Certificate of Destruction / Junk / Parts Only
items.desc: Highest risk for a beginner. Don't evaluate without understanding country, state, export and future registration.

faq.q: Can I submit a request without taking the course?
faq.a: Base lessons are mandatory — they cover the main risks. The rest can be taken in parallel.

faq.q: Why are some lessons mandatory?
faq.a: It protects both sides: you don't submit a request without understanding, and we don't execute bids that hurt the client.

faq.q: Can I buy a car entirely on my own?
faq.a: In Basic — yes, you prepare the lot and the request yourself. The manager just executes the bid within your limit.

faq.q: What does the manager do?
faq.a: Reviews the request, executes the bid in your limit via Car Auctions, oversees payment and logistics after winning.

faq.q: Can the manager block a bid?
faq.a: Yes — if the lot has obvious risks that make the purchase unviable or unsafe.

faq.q: What if I change my mind after picking a car?
faq.a: Up to bid confirmation, you can drop the lot and pick another.

faq.q: Can I switch packages?
faq.a: Yes. We credit the price difference on upgrade within the active package term.

faq.q: Is there support after winning?
faq.a: Yes. All delivery statuses are visible in the dashboard, and the manager answers questions.

directAccess.body: Basic, Pro and Concierge don't get direct dealer access to the internal Car Auctions. This is for process safety: the bid is executed by a manager in the agreed limit.

faq.q: Will I get a Copart login?
faq.a: Direct client access — no. The manager executes bids in your limit. Partner can get their own dealer account after a contract.

faq.q: Can I bid myself?
faq.a: On Basic, Pro and Concierge — no. On Partner — yes, after contract, deposit and vetting.

faq.q: Why doesn't BidBIDDERS open Car Auctions to everyone?
faq.a: It's a professional tool. Without vetting and process understanding it creates major risk for the client and reputational risk for our dealer account.

faq.q: Is there Manheim access?
faq.a: Yes, via the manager. Manheim is a dealer auction — direct client access is closed.

faq.q: Can I buy from Europe?
faq.a: Yes. The base includes BCA and Copart Germany plus other local European platforms.

faq.q: Copart or IAAI — which is better?
faq.a: Depends on the lot. Both are large. The course has a module with examples when one is better than the other.

faq.q: Which auction fits a beginner?
faq.a: Usually Copart or IAAI in the US — they have the most explanation, photos and examples. European platforms come next.

faq.q: Why can a cheap lot be unprofitable?
faq.a: Because the full price includes dozens of additional costs. Module 5 of the course covers this.

emotions.title: Why max bid matters more than emotions
